title: Austin Urban Agenda: Furnace, Fuel, Parks
summary:
*   **Blast Furnace Blocked:** City leaders rejected a permit request to erect a blast furnace at Colorado and 5th streets, signaling early considerations for urban planning and industrial development.
*   **Future Energy Secured:** A new contract for lignite coal was approved for the city's power plant, with provisions anticipating a future transition to power generated from the new Colorado River dam.
*   **Park & City Hall Upgrades:** Funds were reallocated to support improvements at several city parks, including East Avenue, Pease, and Wooldridge Parks, and for general City Hall operations.
*   **Citizen Tax & Fee Relief:** The council remitted impound fees for citizens' cows, with special consideration given to a widow and cases involving new pound limits, and corrected mistaken property and automobile tax assessments.
*   **Delinquent Taxes Pursued:** Legal action was authorized against numerous property owners to collect unpaid taxes, demonstrating the city's enforcement of financial obligations.

Wednesday Aug 21st 1912.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: Councilman
Bartholomew offered the following resolution : Whereas the Rockdale Lignite Co ,Lignite
mine at or near Rockdale,Texas, has taken fire and it has been found necessary to close
the mine to extinguish the fire,which closing may continue for an indefinite time,and,
Contract for
Lignite
Aug 15th 1912-
to
Aug 15th 1913
Awarded
Ryan & Perry
Whereas, said Rockdale Lignite Co has asked to be relieved from its contract to furnish
the City of Austin with Lignite for the Water,Light and Power Plant for the balance of the
year 1912, and Messrs Ryan and Perry of Rockdale ,Texas, have signified their willingness
to carry out the contract with certain qualifications; Now therefore, Resolved that the
Supt of Parks and Public Property be authorized to contract with Messrs Ryan and Perry for
Lignite for the City of Austin, Texas, for the year commencing August 15th 1912, and
ending August 15th 1913, at $1.35 per ton f o b Austin,Texas, under similar contract to
that with the Rockdale Lignite Co; with the proviso that when the City of Austin can
receive power from the dam now being erected across the Colorado River above the City of
Austin ,it shall not be obligated to take only such lignite as shall be required for
additional power ; and provided also that the City of Austin shall have the option of
extending the contract for Lignite with Messrs Ryan & Perry until Jan 1st 1914, upon the
same terms by giving the said Ryan & Perry notice of such desired extension 30 days before
the expiration of the proposed contract.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew,Hart,Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
